transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because… I know this is going to sound hard to explain, but I’ve been really convinced that one of my MBA classmates and a startup advisor are sort of quietly coordinating opportunities for me. Like certain comments in class or Slack messages feel like coded signals about where my career is supposed to go.
Do you think it's possible that you're misinterpreting these comments and messages?

I mean… I guess it’s possible in theory, but it really doesn’t feel that way to me. It feels pretty clear that those comments and Slack messages are meant as signals, like they’re pointing me toward certain career opportunities. I know it sounds unusual, but I’m pretty convinced they’re coordinating it quietly.
How long have you believed that your classmates and the startup advisor are coordinating opportunities for you?
About two months now. It started around when I began the part-time MBA prerequisite program, while I was still working my operations job.
Have you had any other thoughts that you're convinced are true, but that others might find hard to believe?

Mostly that same thing, honestly. I’m really convinced the classmate and the startup advisor are communicating indirectly with me, like through comments in class or Slack messages. It feels like they’re sending coded signals about what opportunities I’m supposed to pursue, even though I know other people might think that sounds hard to believe.
Have you had any other thoughts like this, where you're convinced of something that others might not believe?

Not really anything separate from that. It’s mostly this belief that my MBA classmate and the startup advisor are kind of coordinating things quietly for me. Like, certain comments in class or Slack messages feel coded, like they’re pointing me toward where my career is supposed to go. I know other people might not believe that, but I’ve been pretty convinced of it.
Have your thoughts about your classmate and the startup advisor coordinating opportunities for you ever changed or wavered since you first started believing it?

It’s wavered a little in the sense that I know it sounds hard to explain, and I’ll question how it would look to someone else. But most of the time I’m still convinced it’s happening — like the comments in class or Slack messages feel too specific, like they’re coded signals about where I’m supposed to go next.
Have you ever been convinced of anything else that you thought was true, but others might not believe, outside of this situation with your classmate and the startup advisor?

No, not outside of that situation. It’s really been focused on them — my classmate and the startup advisor — and this feeling that they’re quietly setting things up or sending me signals through class comments or Slack. I know it sounds hard to explain, but that’s the main thing I’ve been convinced of.
Do you believe that the comments or messages from your classmate and the startup advisor are specifically meant for you, or could they be intended for someone else?

I believe they’re meant for me. I know that probably sounds strange, but when my classmate says certain things in class or the advisor posts something in Slack, it feels too specific to just be general. Like they’re signaling what I’m supposed to do next with my career.
Have you ever had any other thoughts that you were completely convinced of, but that might seem strange or unlikely to others?

Not really other things, no. The main thing I’ve been completely convinced of is this situation with my MBA classmate and the startup advisor — that they’re kind of quietly coordinating opportunities for me. Like certain comments in class or Slack messages feel like coded signals about where my career is supposed to go.
Have you ever had any thoughts that you were completely convinced of, but seemed strange or unlikely to others, outside of the situation with your classmate and the startup advisor?

No, not really outside of that. It’s been this one thing — I’ve been really convinced that my MBA classmate and the startup advisor are kind of coordinating things for me, and that some class comments or Slack messages are signals about what I’m supposed to do next career-wise. I know it sounds unlikely, but that’s what I keep coming back to.
Has your belief that your classmate and the startup advisor are coordinating opportunities for you ever completely gone away since you first started believing it?

No, it hasn’t completely gone away. I mean, I can question it a little when I say it out loud, because I know it sounds hard to explain, but I keep coming back to feeling convinced that my classmate and the startup advisor are coordinating these opportunities for me through comments and Slack messages.
Have you ever had any other thoughts that you were completely convinced of, but seemed strange or unlikely to others, at any point in your life?

No, I don’t think so. At any point in my life, it’s really just been this one belief — that my MBA classmate and the startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me, and that some comments in class or Slack messages are like coded signals about where my career should go. I know that probably sounds strange to other people, but I’ve felt really convinced of it.
Have you ever had any other beliefs that you were completely convinced of, despite others thinking they were unlikely or strange?

No, not really any other ones. It’s mainly this same belief I’ve been trying to explain — that my MBA classmate and the startup advisor are sort of quietly arranging opportunities for me, and that certain class comments or Slack messages are meant as signals about what I’m supposed to do next. I know other people probably think that sounds strange, but I’ve felt really convinced about it.
Have you ever had any other beliefs that you were completely convinced of, despite evidence to the contrary?

No, I don’t think there have been other beliefs like that. It’s really this one thing I keep coming back to — that my MBA classmate and the startup advisor are somehow coordinating opportunities for me, and that certain comments or Slack messages are coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. I know other people don’t really see it that way, but I’ve felt very convinced of it.
Have you ever had any other beliefs that you were completely convinced of, and that have lasted for more than a month?

No, I don’t think there’s been another belief like that. The one that’s lasted is the same thing I mentioned — I’ve been really convinced my MBA classmate and that startup advisor are quietly setting up opportunities for me, and that some class comments or Slack messages are meant as signals about where I should go with my career.
Has your belief that your classmate and the startup advisor are coordinating opportunities for you changed in intensity over the past two months?

Yes, it has. It’s been pretty strong the whole time, but over the past couple months I think there are times when it feels more intense — like I’ll see a comment in class or a Slack message and feel really sure it’s a signal for me. Then other times I can step back a little and think, okay, maybe this sounds unlikely. But the belief hasn’t really gone away.
Have you ever felt like you're in danger because of something someone else is doing, even if it didn't seem that way to others?

Not really in danger, no. It’s more that I’ve felt like people were involved in guiding or setting up opportunities for me — especially my MBA classmate and the startup advisor. Like certain comments or Slack messages felt like coded signals about my career. But I wouldn’t say I felt threatened or unsafe because of it.
Have you ever felt like someone else was out to get you or harm you in some way?

No, not like someone was out to get me or trying to harm me. It’s more that I’ve been convinced people — like my MBA classmate and a startup advisor — were quietly coordinating opportunities for me, and that certain class comments or Slack messages were signals about where my career should go. It didn’t feel threatening exactly.
Have you ever felt like someone else was controlling your actions or thoughts?

Not controlling my actions or thoughts, no. It’s more like I feel really convinced that they’re coordinating things around me — like my classmate and the startup advisor — and that comments in class or Slack messages are meant as signals for what I should do with my career. But I don’t feel like they’re making me think or do things directly.
Has your belief that your classmate and the startup advisor are coordinating opportunities for you persisted without any breaks since it first started?

Yes, it’s been pretty constant. I mean, there are times I’m not actively thinking about it, but when it comes up, I still feel convinced it’s real — that my classmate and the startup advisor are coordinating things and that some comments or Slack messages are signals about where I’m supposed to go with my career.
